title: 2015 AMC 12B Problem 10
statement: How many noncongruent integer-sided triangles with positive area and perimeter less than \(15\) are neither equilateral, isosceles, nor right triangles?

solutions.text:
Let the distinct sides be \(a \lt b \lt c.\) Since \(a + b \gt c,\) the perimeter exceeds \(2c,\) so \(2c \lt 15\) and \(c \le 6.\)

The scalene triples with perimeter less than \(15\) are \((6,5,3),\) \((6,5,2),\) \((6,4,3),\) \((5,4,3),\) \((5,4,2),\) and \((4,3,2).\) Of these, only \((5,4,3)\) is a right triangle, leaving \(5.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: With sides \(a \lt b \lt c,\) the triangle inequality gives perimeter \(\gt 2c\)
This forces \(c \le 6;\) list scalene triples and drop the right triangle \(3, 4, 5\)
